Awareness Rooms, developed by GAME NA KIBUN and published by PLAYISM, is a rare kind of puzzle experience that deliberately strips away the player’s sense of familiarity and replaces it with uncertainty. From the moment the game begins, it places you in an unfamiliar environment where even the most basic objects are difficult to interpret, forcing you to confront a world that feels simultaneously ordinary and alien. Instead of guiding you with tutorials or clear objectives, the game leans into disorientation as a design philosophy, asking you not just to solve puzzles but to first understand what you are even looking at. This approach immediately sets it apart from traditional escape room-style titles, as the challenge is rooted as much in perception as it is in logic.

The defining mechanic revolves around the concept of “awareness,” a system that governs how clearly you perceive the environment. At the start, objects are vague, poorly described, and often misleading, with items appearing as abstract shapes or being labeled in simplistic, almost naive terms. Through interaction—examining, using, and experimenting with these objects—your awareness gradually increases, and the world begins to reveal itself with greater clarity. What initially seemed like meaningless clutter transforms into recognizable tools, and previously incomprehensible spaces start to make sense. This progression is deeply satisfying because it creates a layered form of discovery; you are not just unlocking solutions, but unlocking your ability to interpret the world itself.

As you move through the game’s compact set of rooms, the puzzles evolve in tandem with your growing awareness. Early challenges are straightforward, often requiring basic interaction and observation, but later segments introduce more intricate problem-solving that combines item usage, environmental manipulation, and subtle logical connections. The clever twist is that many puzzles cannot even be approached properly until your awareness has reached a certain level, effectively tying progression to comprehension rather than arbitrary barriers. This creates a looping structure where revisiting earlier spaces with improved perception reveals new possibilities, reinforcing the idea that knowledge itself is the key to advancement. When the design clicks, it produces moments of genuine insight that feel earned rather than handed to the player.

The visual presentation plays a crucial role in supporting this concept. The game adopts a minimalist aesthetic that shifts dynamically based on your awareness level, with objects transitioning from indistinct forms into detailed, recognizable items. This visual transformation is more than just cosmetic—it serves as a tangible representation of your progress, making the act of understanding feel physically reflected in the environment. The overall tone is quiet and introspective, with subdued lighting and sparse environments that emphasize isolation. Audio design follows a similarly restrained approach, relying on subtle effects rather than a prominent soundtrack, which helps maintain focus but can also make the experience feel somewhat empty during extended play.

Despite its originality, the game’s central idea does not expand as much as it could over time. The awareness mechanic remains largely consistent throughout, and while it is initially compelling, it begins to lose some of its novelty as the experience continues. Interacting with objects to increase awareness can eventually feel routine, especially when the process becomes predictable. Additionally, the game’s short length means that just as you fully grasp its systems, it is already approaching its conclusion. While this brevity prevents the concept from overstaying its welcome, it also leaves a sense that the idea could have been explored in more depth with additional rooms, mechanics, or variations.

Another point of friction lies in the game’s intentional lack of guidance. While this design choice reinforces the theme of discovery, it can occasionally lead to moments of confusion where progress stalls not because of complex puzzles, but because of unclear interaction points or obscure requirements. Players who enjoy being left to figure things out on their own will likely appreciate this hands-off approach, but others may find it frustrating, particularly when the game’s abstract presentation makes it difficult to identify what actions are even possible.

Even with these limitations, Awareness Rooms remains a memorable and distinctive entry in the indie puzzle space. It succeeds in delivering an experience that feels genuinely different, using its mechanics to explore the idea of perception in a way that few games attempt. Rather than overwhelming players with content or complexity, it focuses on a single concept and executes it with clarity and purpose. The result is a game that feels more like an interactive thought experiment than a conventional puzzle adventure, leaving a lasting impression despite its modest scope.

In the end, Awareness Rooms is best approached with the expectation of a short, concept-driven experience rather than a fully expansive game. It may not offer extensive replay value or mechanical variety, but what it does achieve is a thoughtful and engaging exploration of how understanding shapes interaction. For players interested in unconventional design and introspective gameplay, it provides a unique journey that is both intriguing and quietly satisfying.

Have you ever rubbed your eyes very hard and tried to look around? Feels like you are using someone elses glasses. Awareness Rooms is a cute puzzle style game that prompts you too build your understanding of what surrounds you with consistant observation.

[Visuals]
The design of the game is very neat, as it manages the pixels to create the feeling of blurriness. This idea of being curious is natural when it comes to games in this rpg maker style, wanting to interact with every object possible to see what interesting text will show, so making it part of the level progression is fun.

[Sound Design]
The Sound design is comfortable and relaxing, nothing too notable.

[Gameplay]
The level design can get quite challanging at times. Should be mostly intuitive and doable for most players.

[Notes]
- There is a bug. Once in the game title screen and fullscreen mode, leaving the window will glitch the ui.

[CONCLUSION]
In general, it is a fun game which is worth the short time you will spend on it: 7/10

　少しずつ認識力を高めて部屋からの脱出を目指す。

　徐々に明らかになる周囲の物体と、
　それらを使って暗号や謎解きを行うのがポイント。

[h1] 面白い/評価できるポイント [/h1]
[b] ・分からないものが分かるようになること [/b]
　ゲーム開始時点では認識力が0なため、
　部屋の中にある物体のほとんどがただの四角になっている。

　それらを調べて認識力が高まってくると、
　次第に物体の正体が判明していき、
　正確な姿が分かると正しいアクションを取れるようになる。

　そうしてギミックを解いて部屋から脱出する、
　という流れは未知から既知への感覚を味わえて良い。

[h1] 不満/残念だったポイント [/h1]
[b] ・後半は謎解きがかなり厳しい [/b]
　ヒントの見落としが多いのかもしれないが、
　後半になればなるほど暗号やギミックのヒントがなく、
　ほぼ行き当たりばったりのようなものも多い。

　謎解きの難易度が高いというよりかは、
　作った人の中ではヒント同士が繋がっていているけど、
　プレイする人にはピンと来ない、みたいな雰囲気を感じた。

[b] ・ゲームシステムへの落とし込みが弱い [/b]
　発想はとても面白いと思う、思うのだけど……

　やってる事自体は"同じ場所を何度か調べる"という、
　脱出ゲームでは当たり前のことなので目新しさはない。

　また、同じ場所を複数のアクションで調べる必要もあり、
　とにかく1つのポイントに対してのアクセス回数が多い。

　これらが相まって、謎解きに至るまでが面倒なのはツラい。
　謎解きで詰まったら調べ直しでツラさ倍増まである。

　そのあたりのゲーム体感性がよろしくないは非常に残念。

[h1] 総評やまとめ [/h1]
　徐々に認識できていくという方向性自体は面白いと思うし、
　価格も高くないので興味があれば試してみるのもアリ。

　ボリュームも短いので、軽い気持ちのおやつ感覚がいいかも。

🔥HOT🔥
[b]🗒️Overview🗒️[/b]
Awareness rooms is a short puzzle game where the gimmick is to interact and examine objects to raise awareness and gain an idea of what these objects may be, using them to escape the five rooms this game has to offer. The puzzles escalate in difficulty as you progress through the game, with the rooms also increasing in size which leads to more puzzles in later rooms.

[b]🖋️Finer Details🖋️[/b]
The art style is simple but charming, with the character standing out in the room of blurred objects and as you become more aware, the objects gain colour and shape which gives the objects identity again where you can tell what they are. The art-style is probably my favourite part of the game. The audio is minimal, with small sound effects when interacting with objects or becoming more aware to your surroundings which add to the overall experience of the game.

The puzzle content has some puzzles which may give you a hiccup, although at least in my playthrough were quickly solved. There is some backtracking as well, which links previous levels together. The overall game length will take you around 1 hour maximum, given you get stuck on some puzzles. If you don't the playtime may be even less. As for achievements, 100% will be achieved upon completing the game.

[b]🐜Issues/Bugs🐜[/b]
The main issue which I had when playing was the lack of saving, where you would only get a save when entering a new room, meaning that any progress in between would be lost. This was very frustrating when having to reboot as all objects would need to be interacted and examined again only to get back to where I was. The gimmick of this game becomes stale quick, with it being intuitive and fun at the beginning although tedious in levels such as the last which have several rooms all with different objects, almost becoming a content sponge/time waste rather than a fun part of the gameplay loop.

[b]🥁Closing Statement🥁[/b]
Awareness Rooms is a great bite-sized puzzle game which has a great atmosphere and art-style which add to the overall experience. I do think that the game is slightly expensive given what it provides although I can definitely recommend purchasing the game when its on sale.
